papers.title: Thermocatalytic transcarbonation with diethyl carbonate for valorization of glycerol : recycling siliceous bauxite residue waste components and exploring the potential of sodalite hydroxide reservoir
papers.journal: Repository of the Academy's Library (Library of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences)
papers.abstract: Bauxite residues contain katoites and desilication products (sodalite and cancrinite), which are excellent candidates for Earth-abundant heterogeneous base catalysts from industrial waste sources. For the first time, they were tested in synthetizing the renewable and promising fuel or fuel additive glycerol carbonate for the purpose of recycling glycerol by-products from biodiesel production. Incorporation of silicate was found to enhance the previously established excellent catalytic activity of tricalcium aluminate (Si-free katoite). Performance of sodalites containing four different cage anion-designed (OH, CO3, SO4, Cl) and carbonated cancrinite was determined to a much greater extent by their Brönsted OH content than by the basicity of the caged anions. Direct catalytic use of bauxite residue resulted in a glycerol carbonate yield of over 80%, but it was quickly deactivated due to the limited reusability of many of its most active components (i.e., Si-free and Si-containing katoites, chloride sodalites). However, hydroxysodalites showed excellent reusability, with a glycerol carbonate yield of around 80% even after 5 reuses. The activity of katoites and sodalities overtook that of many complex systems containing relatively rare metals, such as Ni, Cu, Zr, and Ce. Their excellent activity has made it possible to use diethyl carbonate solvent/reagent, which is more favourable in terms of sustainability, instead of the more widely applied dimethyl carbonate, even with as short reaction times as 30–60 min.

papers.title: Hypoxia-responsive supramolecular systems based on macrocycles and self-assembly structures.
papers.abstract: Hypoxia is closely associated with tumor progression, metastasis, therapeutic resistance, and diagnostic challenges. The timely detection of hypoxia in live cancer cells is critical for early cancer diagnosis and for monitoring the effectiveness of anticancer therapies. Recently, there has been growing interest in non-covalent supramolecular design strategies for the development of hypoxia-sensitive sensors and prodrugs. Unlike the widely employed covalent approach, supramolecular chemistry eliminates the need for complex and time-consuming synthetic processes. Instead, the individual components of the sensor autonomously self-assemble into the desired structure. This review provides an overview of hypoxia-targeted and hypoxia-activated supramolecular probes, along with their mechanisms of action in tumor diagnosis and therapy. The supramolecular systems considered are classified according to the use of certain classes of macrocycles. The role of macrocyclic derivatives in the various proposed approaches and the response patterns of hypoxic targets will also be analyzed. Various representatives of the macrocyclic platforms, namely cyclodextrins, cucurbiturils, pillararenes, (thia)calixarenes, due to their properties such as molecular recognition, are used as molecular containers-carriers for pharmaceuticals and bio-organic fluorescent dyes. As a result of complex formation, the photostability and the signal-to-noise ratio of dyes increase. In addition, the solubility of hydrophobic guests in water improves, cytotoxicity is reduced, and targeted delivery promotes the accumulation of drugs/dyes in tumor cells.

papers.title: Nitric oxide in the occurrence and development of ischemic cerebrovascular disease.
papers.abstract: Since nitric oxide is a chemically highly reactive free radical that can act as both an oxidizing agent and a reducing agent, it is assumed that it has diverse effects on biological tissues. Nitric oxide is fundamentally important for the regulation of immune, reproductive and neuromuscular system functions and is the main signaling molecule and effector that can dilate blood vessels and modulate energy metabolism. This review examines the key role of nitric oxide in the mechanisms underlying the response to hypoxia, as well as in the effects of factors induced by hypoxia. The available conflicting information allowed us to conclude that at present, there is no consensus about the role of endogenous nitric oxide in the processes occurring after ischemic cerebrovascular disease.

papers.title: Hyperbaric oxygen for the treatment of traumatic incomplete spinal cord injury: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
papers.abstract: The therapeutic efficacy of hyperbaric oxygen therapy for traumatic incomplete spinal cord injury remains a subject of debate. To comprehensively evaluate the impact of hyperbaric oxygen on motor function, sensory function, and activities of daily living in patients with traumatic incomplete spinal cord injury, we conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis. We performed a comprehensive search across PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and major Chinese databases for randomized controlled trials published through June 2025. A total of 15 randomized controlled trials were included. The pooled results indicated that hyperbaric oxygen therapy significantly improved the American Spinal Injury Association motor score (mean difference = 10.30, 95% confidence interval: 7.70-12.90), the total American Spinal Injury Association sensory score (mean difference = 29.29, 95% confidence interval: 18.82-39.75), the American Spinal Injury Association light touch score (mean difference = 9.84, 95% confidence interval: 6.15-13.53), and the American Spinal Injury Association pinprick score (mean difference = 8.75, 95% confidence interval: 4.40-13.11). Furthermore, hyperbaric oxygen therapy was associated with significant enhancements in the Barthel Index (mean difference = 16.60, 95% confidence interval: 10.51-22.68) and the Functional Independence Measure (mean difference = 17.41, 95% confidence interval: 10.83-23.98). In conclusion, adjunctive hyperbaric oxygen therapy appears to improve motor function, sensory function, and activities of daily living in patients with traumatic incomplete spinal cord injury compared to conventional treatments alone. However, due to methodological limitations and potential publication bias in the included studies, these findings should be interpreted with caution, and further high-quality, multi-center randomized controlled trials are warranted.

papers.title: High levels of nitric oxide and peroxynitrite with protein nitration: a new therapeutic target for gliomas.
papers.abstract: The gap junction signaling pathway is a core hub mediating intercellular communication, which plays a vital role in maintaining tissue homeostasis, and its dysfunction is closely related to glioma. Nitroproteomics studies have shown that protein tyrosine nitration plays an important role in the progression of glioma, and gap junction is one of the significantly enriched nitroprotein signaling pathways in glioma; proteoformics reveals that nitration can produce various proteoforms of related proteins, which have different functional states in different subtypes of glioma, suggesting that nitration may alter the functional states of related proteins in gap junction pathways. When levels of nitric oxide and peroxynitrite (ONOO-) rise, they induce the tyrosine nitration of key proteins in the gap junction pathway; this nitration not only interferes with the function of the gap junction pathway, but also affects other gap junction-linked signaling networks. Forming an attack network on the gap junction pathway through multi-pathway cross-regulation has great potential for therapeutic strategies targeting the gap junction pathway. We recommend in-depth studies of the gap junction signaling pathway and potential drugs targeting gap junction signals, including drugs that target gap junction communication activators, nitration inhibitors, and drugs that directly target specific nitroproteins, combined with conventional chemotherapy or immune checkpoint inhibitors, as well as the construction of personalized medical frameworks as important future research directions.

papers.title: Antitrust Regulation of Algorithmic "Platform-Driven Involution'': From Governing the Corporate Person to Governing the Platform Ecosystem
papers.abstract: Digital platforms increasingly govern competition through algorithmically administered rules that allocate visibility, subsidies, commissions, participation opportunities, and sanctions. This article reconstructs ``platform-driven involution'' as a testable, portfolio-based theory-of-harm framework rather than a freestanding antitrust offense. Its application remains anchored in market definition, dominance, identified conduct under Article 22 of China's Anti-Monopoly Law, causal proof, competitive effects, and objective justification. The article clarifies that ecosystem analysis supplements rather than replaces relevant-market analysis and develops an evidence architecture for separating platform-induced effects from macroeconomic, demand, cost, and merchant-specific confounders. It then distinguishes preventive measures already supported by Chinese hard law or voluntary compliance guidance from compulsory competition-specific filing and pre-deployment assessment that would require clearer future authorization. The 2026 Trip.com decision is used to show how traffic allocation, exclusivity, lowest-price requirements, technical monitoring, and sanctions can form an integrated abuse architecture while liability remains tied to established statutory categories. Comparative analysis of EU platform regulation and Google Shopping supports calibrated procedural prevention, meaningful explanation, and causal discipline without protecting inefficient competitors or condemning aggressive competition.

The 2026 Trip.com decision is used to show how traffic allocation, exclusivity, lowest-price requirements, technical monitoring, and sanctions can form an integrated abuse architecture while liability remains tied to established statutory categories.

papers.title: Digital-Twin-Driven Predictive Maintenance and Fault-Tolerant Control for Electrified Agricultural Machinery: A Multiphysics and Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework for PMSM In-Wheel Drives
papers.abstract: Electrified agricultural machinery increasingly relies on permanent-magnet synchronous motor drives that must remain dependable under variable traction, terrain-induced vibration, thermal cycling, contamination, and intermittent duty. Existing work offers mature methods for motor fault diagnosis, digital twins, predictive maintenance, and distributed-drive fault-tolerant control, but their health information is often not shared across diagnosis, maintenance, and control. This article develops a multiphysics digital-twin framework in which electrical, thermal, mechanical, and vibrational evidence maintains a probabilistic health belief that constrains both supervisory maintenance decisions and torque redistribution. The framework formalizes observability, uncertainty-aware health factors, deterministic safety shielding, multi-rate fallback logic, and agriculture-specific traction constraints. Reproducible low-fidelity numerical studies provide preliminary support for context-conditioned residual diagnosis and the revised thermal-continuity trade-off underlying health-aware derating, including robustness and sensitivity analyses. They do not validate sim-to-real transfer or the reinforcement-learning policy itself; those hypotheses remain open for dynamometer and hardware-in-the-loop testing. The results are therefore interpreted as mechanism-level evidence rather than field-performance validation.

The results are therefore interpreted as mechanism-level evidence rather than field-performance validation.

papers.title: Current status of room temperature magnetic compensation in impurity-doped Mn4N epitaxial thin films
papers.abstract: Mn4N, a ferrimagnet that does not contain rare-earth elements, possesses attractive properties for spintronics applications. In particular, Mn4N epitaxial films exhibit a small spontaneous magnetization of about 100 kA m(-1), a large spin polarization (p = 0.8), and large perpendicular magnetic anisotropy with a magnetic anisotropy constant of approximately 10(5) J m(-3). More importantly, achieving magnetic compensation at room temperature is possible through impurity doping. This property is particularly significant for spin-torque-based spintronics applications. In the vicinity of the magnetization and/or angular momentum compensation points, magnetization dynamics can be substantially accelerated, enabling high-speed switching and domain wall motion. This article surveys the magnetic properties of impurity-doped Mn4N epitaxial films grown on SrTiO3(001) substrates, highlighting recent results obtained with Cu-, Ag-, Au-, and Pd-doped Mn4N films in comparison with Ni- and Cr-doped Mn4N films. Furthermore, with a view to device applications of Mn4N, we present the formation of ultrathin (similar to 4 nm) Pt epitaxial films with a <100> orientation on MgO (001), which is essential for injecting spins into Mn4N-based overlayers by utilizing the spin Hall effect of heavy metals. papers.title: Reproducible chiroptical activity from aggregated chiral thienopyrroledione-fluorene π-conjugated polymers
papers.abstract: Chiral pi-conjugated polymers have attracted considerable interest because their chiral-aggregated structures can generate pronounced chiroptical responses. Here, we report the design, synthesis, and chiroptical characterization of fluorene - thienopyrroledione polymers bearing a single chiral center in each repeating unit, (R)- and (S)-PFTPD, prepared via direct arylation polycondensation to minimize structural defects. Although only weak chiroptical activity was observed in the solution, the addition of 1-butanol to CHCl3 solutions of the polymers induced the formation of stable aggregates that exhibited strong circular dichroism (CD) and circularly polarized luminescence (CPL). Systematic examination of the sample preparation parameters revealed that the mixing process critically influences the chiroptical properties. Dropwise addition of 1-butanol under controlled stirring provided the most reliable results, yielding highly reproducible CD spectra. Under these optimized conditions, the aggregates exhibited an average dissymmetry factor (|g abs|) of 1.5 & times; 10-2 and a CPL dissymmetry factor (|g lum|) of 1.9 & times; 10-2. These values rank among the highest reported for pi-conjugated polymer aggregates bearing only a single chiral source per repetition unit. This study demonstrates that precise control over the solvent-mixing process is essential for the reproducible emergence of chiroptical properties and highlights the chiral TPD unit as a promising platform for chiroptical polymer materials.

papers.title: DIAGNOSTIC ACCURACY OF ULTRA-LOW-DOSE CT VS. STANDARD-DOSE CT FOR PULMONARY NODULE DETECTION: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW AND META-ANALYSIS
authors: KHALED BONNA , RASHA GALAL ELSAFTY , NORA EID ALANAZI , RANIN JABER M ALMAJRASHI AHLAM ALI Y ASIRI , WALEED MUFAREH ALSHAHRANI , SOMAYYAH SOHAIL MITHA , SHOUG NASSER ALKHAMMASH , BANDAR SAAD ALSHREEF
papers.journal: TPM Testing, psychometrics, methodology in applied psychology
papers.abstract: Background: Standard dose computed tomography (CT) is a primary modality for detecting pulmonary nodules (PNs), but the health risk from cumulative radiation exposure has prompted the emergence of ultra-low-dose CT (ULDCT) as an alternative to reduce this dose, because its diagnostic accuracy remains variable, this systematic review and meta-analysis aims to synthesize the existing evidence to determine the diagnostic accuracy and effective radiation dose of ULDCT for pulmonary nodule detection. Methods: Following PRISMA guidelines, a systematic search was conducted in PubMed, Cochrane Library, and Ovid MEDLINE for original research published between 2015 and 2025 that evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of ULDCT for PN detection, for which a meta-analysis using random-effects models was performed to calculate the pooled sensitivity for nodule detection and the pooled mean effective radiation dose, with a subgroup analysis conducted to assess the impact of different reconstruction algorithms. Results: Forty-two studies comprising 15,792 patients were included, from which a meta-analysis of 11 studies demonstrated a pooled sensitivity of 91.9% (95% CI: 84.6%–97.1%) for PN detection with heterogeneity (I²=93.0%), and a pooled mean effective dose from 12 studies of 0.22 mSv (95% CI: 0.11–0.33 mSv), a level comparable to standard chest radiography, while subgroup analysis revealed a trend towards higher sensitivity with advanced reconstruction algorithms (96.7%) compared to standard iterative reconstruction (87.9%) that was not statistically significant (p=0.091), and a narrative synthesis confirmed ULDCT's accuracy for solid nodules but identified reduced sensitivity for subsolid, ground-glass, and small (<6 mm) nodules, with performance limited in patients with a high body mass index (BMI). Conclusion: ULDCT combined with advanced reconstruction techniques offers high diagnostic accuracy for the detection of solid pulmonary nodules and reduces radiation exposure to levels approaching that of a chest X-ray, but its utility is limited for detecting subsolid and small nodules and in obese patients, making protocol standardization and patient-specific considerations essential to optimize its clinical implementation.

papers.title: Efficient deoxygenation of palm oil to green diesel using a metal oxide catalysts supporting on ZrO2-enhanced graphene oxide
papers.journal: Universiti Putra Malaysia Institutional Repository (Universiti Putra Malaysia)
papers.abstract: NiO, Fe2O3, and bimetallic oxide NiFe2O4 catalysts supported on graphene oxide and promoted with ZrO2 were synthesized via wet-impregnation approach. A systematic characterization of the catalysts physicochemical properties was evaluated using X-ray diffraction (XRD), Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR), Temperature-programmed desorption CO2 (TPD-CO2), Brunaur-Emmett-Teller (BET) surface area, Field emission Scanning electron microscopy (FESEM), and Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) analysis. The catalysts were evaluated as heterogeneous catalysts in the deoxygenation (DO) of palm oil for green diesel production under varying operating conditions. Among the catalysts tested, Fe2O3/ZrO2-GO (calcined at 400 °C for 4 h, 5 wt% loading) demonstrated superior catalytic activity, achieving a maximum hydrocarbon yield (HC%) of 98.0%, bio-jet fuel (BJF) selectivity of 40%, and kerosene yield of 86%. The exceptional performance is attributed to the catalyst’s large BET surface area (18.64 m2/g), substantial pore volume (0.027 cm3 /g), and moderate surface basicity (3234.65 μmol/g), which collectively facilitate efficient deoxygenation via decarboxylation (DCO2) and decarbonylation (DCO) pathways while suppressing undesired cracking. Furthermore, the catalyst exhibited remarkable stability and reusability over four consecutive reaction cycles, retaining 92% hydrocarbon yield and 80.9% kerosene yield, with BJF selectivity increasing to 84%. The gradual decline in performance is attributed to carbon deposition (coke formation), pore blockage, and sintering-induced degradation of the mesoporous network, as confirmed by post-reaction XRD and BET analysis.

papers.title: Passive Thermal Management of Electric Vehicle Batteries Using Enhanced Phase Change Materials
papers.journal: Indian Journal of Science and Technology
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: This research aims to create, improve, and test a passive thermal management system (TMS) for lithium-ion EV batteries. The goal is to keep cell temperatures below 50°C during high-rate discharges without using extra power. The study focuses on improving the low thermal conductivity of standard phase change materials (PCMs) by developing a composite with expanded graphite (EG) and evaluating its ability to reduce thermal runaway risks and temperature differences within the battery module. Methods: To make the composite PCM, 20% expanded graphite was added to commercial paraffin wax (RT42) using a vacuum process to keep the structure strong and reduce empty spaces. The team measured its properties using Differential Scanning Calorimetry (DSC) and the transient plane source method. They tested the material in an 8-cell LG Chem M50S module set up in a 2×2×2 cube. The tests included constant-rate discharges (1C to 5C), high-current pulses (3C) to mimic acceleration and braking, and a long-term test of 500 charge-discharge cycles. Findings: The optimized EG-PCM composite exhibited a thermal conductivity of 5.9 W/m·K, a 29.5-fold increase over pure paraffin, while maintaining a latent heat capacity of 182 J/g. Module-level testing at a 2C discharge rate and 25°C ambient temperature showed a 50% reduction in peak cell temperatures (38.2°C) compared to the air-cooled baseline (52.3°C). Temperature uniformity improved to ±1.1°C, closely matching the performance of active liquid-cooled systems (±0.3°C). Long-term cycling demonstrated stable latent heat capacity, with no significant material degradation or accelerated battery ageing over 500 cycles. Novelty: This study stands out because it fully tests a high-conductivity composite PCM under sudden fault conditions, like 3C pulse discharges that mimic thermal spikes before a short circuit. Unlike earlier research that focused only on material production or steady-state tests, this work includes long-term reliability data (500 cycles) and a cost analysis. It shows a calculated thermal buffer of ~28°C below the nominal thermal runaway onset temperature (~70°C) under tested conditions. Abuse testing was not conducted. Keywords: Phase Change Materials (PCM), Lithium-Ion Battery, Passive Thermal Management, Expanded Graphite Composite (EG), Thermal Runaway Prevention, Electric Vehicles (EV)

papers.title: Phosphorylated Chitosan‐Based Ionogels for Quasi‐Solid‐State Supercapacitors With Activated Carbon Electrodes
papers.abstract: Although liquid electrolytes are widely used in electrochemical energy‐storage devices, they present leakage, safety, and packaging challenges. This work investigates a phosphorylated chitosan/1‐ethyl‐3‐methylimidazolium dicyanamide (PCS/EMIMDCA) ionogel as a fluorine‐free quasi‐solid‐state electrolyte for supercapacitors. The phosphorylated chitosan formed a homogeneous, nonleaking ionogel film up to 80 wt% EMIMDCA. FTIR band shifts were consistent with hydrogen‐bonding and ion‐dipole interactions between EMIMDCA and the phosphorylated chitosan matrix. DSC analysis showed suppression of bulk EMIMDCA crystallization over the investigated temperature range, while the main thermal‐decomposition step began at approximately 220 °C. The optimized PCS:EMIMDCA ionogel achieved an ionic conductivity of 5.3 ± 0.3 mS cm −1 at 30 °C and a full‐cell operating voltage of 1.8 V. When assembled in a symmetric activated carbon (AC//PCS:EMIMDCA//AC) device, it delivered a specific capacitance of 28 F g −1 at 1 A g −1 , a specific energy of 9.6 Wh kg −1 and an average specific power of 0.75 kW kg −1 . In long‐term cycling, the ionogel‐based device retained 76% of its initial capacitance after 10,000 cycles, which represents over twice the stability of the neat EMIMDCA system. These results identify phosphorylated chitosan/EMIMDCA ionogels as durable, fluorine‐free electrolytes based on a bio‐derived polymer host, with improved cycling stability compared with neat EMIMDCA.

papers.title: Topical Delivery Enhancement Of Luliconazole Via Liposomal Gel: Design, Characterization And For Skin Fungal Infection
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Background: The imidazole antifungal drug luliconazole is used to treat fungal infections, but it has a poor skin penetration rate and is quickly removed from the body.Materials and Procedures: Luliconazole liposomes were created via thin-film hydration and added to carbopol gel.For lipid ratio, cholesterol content, and hydration time, nine formulations (F1-F9) were created and refined.Studies were conducted in comparison with marketed formulation.Results: When compared to commercially available gel, the prepared liposomal gel displayed consistent drug content, nanosized vesicles, and prolonged drug release.The efficiency of entrapment reached 82.3%.Longer, slower release was confirmed by Franz diffusion studies.Conclusion: Long-lasting therapeutic effects, enhanced skin retention, decreased dosage frequency, and patient compliance are all provided by liposomal gel of luliconazole.

papers.title: Experimental evaluation of nano-PCM based thermal energy storage for solar drying applications: Drying kinetics, heat transfer, Differential Scanning Calorimetry (DSC), and quality characteristics
papers.journal: Solar Energy Materials and Solar Cells
papers.abstract: This study presents a novel controlled experimental comparison of paraffin wax phase change material (PCM) and zinc oxide nanoparticle-enhanced paraffin wax (ZnO-PCM) integrated into a solar drying system for potato chips under identical meteorological conditions. Unlike previous studies that investigated PCM and Nano-PCM systems independently, this work systematically quantifies their relative effects on drying kinetics, heat and mass transfer, thermodynamic performance, and product quality. Experiments were conducted in three operating modes: Category-I (without PCM), Category-II (PCM), and Category-III (ZnO-PCM). The initial moisture content (80-88%) decreased to final values of 11-12%, 9-10%, and 6-8% for Category-I, Category-II, and Category-III, respectively, after 21 h of drying. The moisture ratio reduced from 1.0 to 0.10-0.12, 0.08-0.10, and 0.05-0.08, respectively. The maximum drying efficiency increased from 34% in Category-I to 39% and 42% in Category-II and Category-III, respectively. The effective moisture diffusivity ranged from 4.5 × 10 −10 to 6.8 × 10 −10 m 2 /s in Category-I and increased up to 8.5 × 10 −10 m 2 /s in Category-III. The mass transfer coefficient varied between 1.2 × 10 −7 and 4.2 × 10 −7 m/s, while the heat transfer coefficient increased from 8 to 18 W/m 2 K in Category-I to 12-28 W/m 2 K in Category-III. The activation energy was found to be 21.5-30.5 kJ/mol, and water activity decreased from 0.98 to 0.32-0.45. The total color difference (ΔE) was lowest for Category-III (23.50), compared with Category-II (25.20) and Category-I (29.20), indicating superior color retention. Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) observations further suggested better preservation of the microstructure in ZnO-PCM-dried samples. Overall, the incorporation of ZnO-PCM significantly enhanced thermal energy storage, heat and mass transfer, drying kinetics, and product quality. These findings demonstrate the potential of Nano-PCM-assisted thermal energy storage as an efficient and sustainable solution for improving solar drying performance and preserving the quality of agricultural products.

papers.title: Investigation of the dosimetric characteristics of real-time silicone/Bi2O3 nanocomposites for the diagnostic level X-rays
papers.abstract: Abstract This study presents the development of high-sensitivity real-time X-ray dosimeters based on room-temperature-vulcanized (RTV-2) silicone nanocomposites incorporating 0–60 wt% Bi 2 O 3 nanoparticles, fabricated via solution casting. Structural and morphological characterization using X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) with elemental mapping, and elemental analysis confirmed the uniform dispersion of monoclinic Bi 2 O 3 nanorods within the amorphous RTV-2 matrix. Complementary Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), Raman spectroscopy, and thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) validated the chemical integrity, thermal stability, and mechanical robustness of the resulting nanocomposites. Dosimetric performance was investigated under diagnostic-range X-ray exposure using a COMET MXR 320/26 source (dose rates: 2.8–12 mGy/min). The I-V characteristics at 4.8 mGy/min exhibited a highly linear response over ± 400 V. At 400 V, the photocurrent increased from ~ 0.56 nA (pure RTV-2) to ~ 1.66 nA (60 wt% Bi 2 O 3 ), corresponding to a ~ 3-fold enhancement in photocurrent. The devices demonstrated good short-term repeatability (standard deviation of 2.3% over ten consecutive measurements) and a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of up to ~ 1900 at 400 V. Compared with reported values for commercial MOSFET dosimeters (~ 0.1–1 nA/mGy) and previously reported Bi 2 O 3 -polymer systems, the developed nanocomposites exhibit a higher competitive normalized sensitivity (~ 0.35 nA/(mGy/min), or 878 nC·mGy⁻ 1 ·cm⁻ 3 on a volumetric basis), demonstrating their suitability as lead-free alternatives for low-dose, real-time diagnostic X-ray dosimetry; further evaluation of long-term stability and mechanical durability is needed to establish clinical applicability.

papers.title: Efficient Propranolol Delivery Enabled by Manganese‐Based Bioactive Metal–Organic Frameworks With High Loading Capacity
papers.abstract: A green and efficient method was developed for propranolol delivery utilizing manganese‐based bioactive metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) as biocompatible drug carriers. Mn‐based bioactive MOFs with a high aspect ratio were synthesized and characterized for size (average, 17 µm), morphology, stability, elemental composition, crystallinity, functionality, charge character, and biocompatibility (a protein adsorption capacity of 0.03 µg µg −1 (5 h) and a hemolysis ratio of < 0.5%). Afterward, the MOFs were utilized for drug loading via an encapsulation method, and the drug release studies were also performed. The drug loading was confirmed using the zeta potential, CHN analysis, and thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) measurements. An encapsulation efficiency of 96% (0.5 W/W (drug/MOFs)) and a maximal capacity ( Q max ) of 0.526 mg mg −1 were obtained. The drug release showed that 93.72% of the loaded drug was released after 10 h for a composite of 0.25 W/W (drug/MOFs), while for 0.5 W/W (drug/MOFs), the drug release reached a plateau after 3 h. The kinetic studies showed longer release times and higher release rates for higher drug loading efficiency. Overall, herein, a bioactive platform for efficient delivery of propranolol was developed to improve the therapeutic efficacy by enhancing the drug loading and achieving controlled drug release.

papers.title: Bilayer Tablet Technology in Ayush Systems: Formulation Strategies, Challenges, and Quality Evaluation of Herbal–Herbo Mineral Dosage Forms
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Ayush medicines are increasingly being modernized through the integration of advanced pharmaceutical technologies to enhance patient compliance, dosing precision, and product stability.While bilayer tablet technology has been extensively explored in allopathic systems, its application in traditional medicine remains underdeveloped.The incorporation of Herbal -Herbo mineral components into bilayer tablet systems presents unique challenges, including interfacial adhesion between layers, structural instability due to elastic recovery, and variability in phytochemical composition.This review critically examines formulation strategies, mechanical considerations, physicochemical characterization techniques (including FTIR, DSC, XRPD, and ICP-OES), and Quality by Design (QbD) approaches relevant to the development of Herbal -Herbo mineral bilayer tablets.Particular emphasis is placed on interfacial integrity, crystallinity changes, elemental profiling, and drug release kinetics modelling.Furthermore, the challenges and limitations associated with adapting traditional combination dosage forms into bilayer tablet systems are discussed.This review also identifies key research gaps and proposes future directions for the scientific validation and global acceptability of Ayush-based bilayer tablet formulations.

papers.title: Electron-beam crosslinking of flame-retardant LDPE/EVA composites: Effects of metal hydroxides and zinc borate on fire and mechanical performance
papers.abstract: Electron-beam (EB) irradiation provides an initiator-free route for modifying highly filled polymer systems, but the combined influence of radiation-induced network formation and halogen-free flame-retardant formulation remains insufficiently understood. This study investigates dose-dependent EB effects on LDPE/EVA composites containing aluminum trihydroxide (ATH), magnesium hydroxide (MH), and zinc borate (ZB) for cable-insulation applications. Composites containing 60–64 wt% inorganic fillers were irradiated at 0–250 kGy and evaluated by gel-content, hot-set, thermogravimetric, tensile, limiting oxygen index (LOI), smoke-density, and cone-calorimetry measurements. Increasing EB dose promoted progressive network formation, evidenced by increased gel content and improved hot-set performance, and was accompanied by enhanced dimensional stability and tensile-strength retention. Fire performance also improved, with LOI increasing from approximately 26%–28% in non-irradiated materials to 31%–34% at higher doses, together with reduced smoke generation and heat release. MH-containing composites generally showed lower smoke-density and heat-release parameters than corresponding ATH-based systems. ZB-containing formulations exhibited further reductions in smoke and heat release and more consolidated post-combustion residues; however, because ZB addition increased total inorganic content from 60 to 64 wt%, these differences cannot be attributed exclusively to an independent ZB effect. Overall, MH/ZB-containing systems at moderate-to-high EB doses showed the most favorable combined network, fire, and mechanical response, demonstrating that absorbed dose and flame-retardant composition act as coupled design variables in highly filled LDPE/EVA composites.

papers.title: Interfacial engineering, processing, and microstructure relationships in PLA/Diss fiber biocomposites for improved mechanical performance
papers.abstract: This study reports the development of fully bio-based polylactic acid (PLA) biocomposites reinforced with short Ampelodesmos mauritanicus (Diss) fibers using a powder-based processing route. To improve fiber-matrix compatibility, the fibers were subjected to sequential HCl/NaOH treatment to modify their surface morphology. A fixed concentration of 10 wt.% was selected to isolate the effect of surface treatment on fiber-matrix interaction rather than to optimize the reinforcement level. Multiscale characterization using SEM, AFM, FTIR, Raman spectroscopy, and DSC showed that the treatment improved interfacial adhesion by promoting mechanical interlocking and molecular interactions between PLA and the exposed cellulose-rich fiber surface. AFM observations confirmed a marked increase in surface roughness, while DSC analysis revealed that treated fibers influenced PLA crystallization through the combined effects of heterogeneous nucleation and restricted chain mobility at the interface. These microstructural changes enhanced load transfer, with the treated-fiber composite reaching a Young’s modulus of 4.24 GPa and a tensile strength of 46.8 MPa. The powder-processing route also promoted homogeneous fiber dispersion and may help reduce thermal and shear-induced degradation compared with conventional melt processing. Overall, the results demonstrate that combining interfacial engineering with powder processing provides an effective strategy for designing lightweight, high-performance, and sustainable PLA/Diss biocomposites.

papers.title: MXene ‐ MWCNTs Hybrid Reinforced PA6 Nanocomposites for Electronic Packaging Applications
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT MXene is considered a promising 2D material for advanced thermal management, flexible electronics, and conductive polymer nanocomposites due to its high electrical conductivity, layered morphology, and tunable surface chemistry. In the present work, various MXene‐based hybrid fillers were prepared by functionalizing Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene with multiwalled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs) in different ratios, namely M4C1, M2C1, and M1C1. The complete structural and microstructural characterization was performed to confirm the successful formation of the hybrids and to study the effect of the filler composition on the electrical transport properties. The MXene–MWCNTs hybrids showed the formation of a 3D interconnecting network between the MXene sheets and the MWCNTs. The charge transport behavior of the hybrid powders was affected by the existence of multiple contact interfaces. Moreover, the optimized hybrid filler (M4C1) was incorporated into a polyamide‐6 (PA6) matrix to prepare PA6–M4C1 nanocomposites. Structural analysis revealed that the semi‐crystalline nature of PA6 was preserved after incorporation of the MXene–MWCNTs hybrid filler; however, the degree of crystallinity was slightly decreased. The PA6–M4C1 nanocomposite showed a considerable increase in electrical conductivity due to the formation of a 3D interconnecting conductive network, which was enabled by the MWCNTs bridging in the polymer matrix. PA6‐based nanocomposites are widely applied in fields such as prevention of electrostatic discharge in electronic packaging, but also show potential for enhanced multifunctional performance. The present study shows that the MXene–MWCNTs hybrid systems are promising materials for the development of electrically conductive polymer nanocomposites for advanced electronic packaging applications.

papers.title: Effects of N‐(4‐Hydroxyphenyl)Maleimide Grafting and Rubber Epoxidation on the Morphology, Viscoelasticity, and Performance of Natural Rubber/Polypropylene Thermoplastic Vulcanizates
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Four thermoplastic vulcanizates (TPVs) with a 50/50 rubber/polypropylene (PP) weight ratio—natural rubber (NR)/PP, epoxidized natural rubber containing 25 mol% epoxide (ENR‐25)/PP, N‐(4‐hydroxyphenyl)maleimide‐grafted NR (NR‐ g ‐HPM)/PP, and HPM‐grafted ENR‐25 (ENR‐25‐ g ‐HPM)/PP—were prepared by dynamic vulcanization using phenolic‐modified PP (PhHRJ‐PP) as a compatibilizer. FTIR confirmed the presence of imide, aromatic, and phenolic functional groups derived from HPM. SEM showed that HPM grafting refined the morphology of the vulcanized rubber, decreasing the mean rubber‐domain size from 2.715 to 2.109 μm for the NR‐based TPVs and from 3.488 to 3.113 μm for the ENR‐25‐based TPVs. The NR‐ g ‐HPM/PP exhibited the best overall balance of mechanical properties. Compared with the unmodified NR/PP counterpart, its tensile strength increased from 11.35 to 13.25 MPa, elongation at break increased from 351.2% to 368.8%, and tension set decreased from 30% to 28%. In contrast, ENR‐25‐ g ‐HPM/PP exhibited the highest oil resistance and thermal stability, with only 3.70% swelling in engine oil and a first‐stage degradation temperature of 411.27°C, compared with 12.50% swelling and 388.80°C, respectively, for the NR/PP TPV. Thus, HPM‐grafted NR offers a more favorable balance of toughness and elastic recovery, while HPM‐grafted ENR‐25 is better suited for TPV applications that require enhanced oil resistance and thermal stability.

papers.title: FORMULATION AND CHARACTERIZATION OF ITRACONAZOLE TABLETS FROM NANOSUSPENSION
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Itraconazole, a broad-spectrum antifungal agent, exhibits poor aqueous solubility, limiting its oral bioavailability.This study aimed to enhance the solubility and therapeutic efficacy of itraconazole by developing a nanosuspension-based tablet formulation for sustained release.The nanosuspension was prepared using the antisolvent precipitation method, followed by high-shear homogenization and ultrasonication.The optimized nanosuspension (F4) was spray-dried into nanogranules and compressed into tablets containing various polymers including HPMC K100, Carbopol 934, and Eudragit RL.The optimized formulation (F6) containing HPMC K100 demonstrated superior sustained release properties, achieving 99.27% drug release over 12 hours following zero-order kinetics.Characterization studies confirmed nanoscale particle size (307 nm), uniformity, and stability with a zeta potential of -30.5 ± 2.84 mV.The FTIR and DSC analyses indicated no significant drug-excipient interactions and confirmed thermal stability.The developed nanosuspension-based itraconazole tablet presents a promising approach for improving solubility, bioavailability, and sustained antifungal efficacy of poorly soluble drugs.

papers.title: Engineering SAN-core architecture in waterborne acrylic latexes for paper coating applications
papers.abstract: Waterborne dispersion coatings are a potential alternative to extrusion coating and lamination for paper-based food packaging, but require latexes that combine barrier performance, film formation, and industrial processability. Here, poly(styrene- co -acrylonitrile) (SAN) was explored as the hard core of film-forming core–shell latexes. Latexes with SAN cores and a soft styrene–acrylic shell were synthesized by seeded semi-batch emulsion polymerization, an industrially established process, varying the acrylonitrile (AN) content of the core (0–75 wt%, at 35 wt% core) and the core fraction (35–65 wt%, at 50 wt% AN). Free-standing films and coated papers (10 μm) were characterized by TEM, SEM, AFM, DSC and TGA, tensile testing, water vapor transmission rate (WVTR), contact angle, and water and oil Cobb 1800 test. The cores remained phase-separated, well dispersed across the AN series but aggregated at high core fractions. All films in the AN series exhibited high flexibility, with elongations at break above 800%, whereas the increase of the core fraction promoted core aggregation and, at 65 wt% core, resulted in brittle films with an elongation at break of only 2%. All coatings reduced the WVTR (434 g m −2 d −1 ) and water uptake (51.3 g m −2 ) of the paper. The shell alone gave the lowest values (30 g m −2 d −1 and 3.0 g m −2 ), closely followed by the 25 wt% AN core (32 g m −2 d −1 and 4.2 g m −2 ), whereas AN content ≥50 wt% (54–71 g m −2 d −1 ) and core aggregation (up to 181 g m −2 d −1 ) compromised the water vapor barrier. For most formulations, the cores reduced oil uptake from 9.2 g m −2 (shell alone) to 3.4–4.7 g m −2 . Cores containing up to 25 wt% AN therefore largely preserve the water barrier properties of the shell while improving its oil resistance.

papers.title: Hybrid zwitterionic biochar-PES-SPAES composite membranes for efficient treatment of antibiotic-laden municipal wastewater
papers.abstract: Antibiotic accumulation in discharged water is a growing global public health concern that demands high-performance membrane materials to mitigate it. Herein, functionalized zwitterionic biochar (ZBC) was incorporated into a novel membrane composite of polyethersulfone/sulfonated poly(arylene ether sulfone) (PES/SPAES) via the phase-inversion process. Several instrumental characterizations confirmed the fabrication of the composite membrane and the incorporation of the nanofiller into its matrix. ZBC integration altered the membrane morphology, pore structure, hydrophilicity, and surface charge, as well as the thermal and mechanical properties. The best-performing composite membrane achieved an outstanding 99.1% tetracycline (TC) removal efficiency at a permeation flux of 64.1 L m −2 h −1 . The membrane maintained its high performance across complex environments, including mixed-antibiotic solutions (98.5%) and antibiotic-loaded real municipal wastewater (94.8%). The membrane exhibited strong antifouling behavior, long-term operation, and high rejection of natural organic matter (NOM). Feed pH variation confirmed its effect on TC separation, achieving superior TC removal under acidic and alkaline conditions (99.9%), with an enhanced flux of 71.8 L m −2 h −1 at pH 3. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations supported the experimental findings, showing enhanced TC–membrane interaction in the PES/SPAES/ZBC system through reduced energy gap, increased electron-transfer capacity, and stable TC-bound configurations. These findings establish ZBC nanofiller and PES/SPAES composite as promising materials for developing high-performance composite membranes for antibiotic removal.

papers.title: Development and Optimization of Nepafenac-Loaded Niosomal Gel for Topical Anti-Inflammatory Delivery: A Quality-by-Design Approach
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Nepafenac, a class II non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) under the biopharmaceutics classification system (BCS), has poor aqueous solubility and dose-limiting gastrointestinal toxicity with oral administration, hence limiting its effective clinical use in musculoskeletal conditions. So, this study was planned to develop, optimize, and characterize a nepafenac-loaded, niosome-based gel for sustained topical drug delivery to bypass its first-pass metabolism and systemic adverse effects. Niosomes were made with the non-ionic surfactant (Span 60) and cholesterol as bilayer-forming agents. The in vitro Span 60 and cholesterol level-dependent formulation of niosomal nepafenac was optimized using a two-factor, three-level (3) factorial design by employing the following independent variables, Span 60 (A) and cholesterol (B), and vesicle size (VS) and entrapment efficiency (EE) as the dependent variables. Preformulation studies of the drug included organoleptic evaluation, melting point, solubility analysis, UV spectrophotometry, and FTIR compatibility studies to establish identity, purity, and excipient compatibility. Nine niosome batches (F1–F9) were characterized for niosome particle morphology, size, polydispersity index (PDI), ZP, and EE. Both responses fitted quadratic models with high adjusted R2 values of 0.8804 and 0.8516, respectively. The optimized niosome batch F5 showed a VS of 356.2 10.2 nm, PDI of 0.298±0.016, ZP of 31.6±1.7 mV, and EE of 88.4±1.9%. The Formulation F5 was loaded into Carbopol 934 gel base (at four levels of 1.0, 1.25, 1.5, and 1.75%w/v) and evaluated with the gel base G3 (1.5%w/v of polymer) exhibiting suitable viscosity (8450±134 cPs), spreadability (10.8±0.5 g cm/s), and drug content (97.6±0.8%) using in vitro studies, G3 releases the nepafenac in a controlled manner to the tune of 76.8±2.1% than the plain drug gel (96.8±3.4%) after 12 h following Korsmeyer-Peppas model with non Fickian anomalous (n = 0.726) transport. DSC confirmed the amorphous state of the drug and intermolecular interactions within the niosomal bilayer, consistent with sustained drug release. The stability study of the optimized gel formulation for 6 months under accelerated storage indicates its stability. These niosomes are a novel vesicular carrier for sustained topical delivery of nepafenac and might be a potential drug delivery platform.

papers.title: Design and Evaluation of Multi-Stimuli-Responsive Nanoparticles for Targeted Drug Delivery in Chronic Diseases
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: The key reasons for disease and death global, cancer, diabetes mellitus, cardiovascular, chronic inflammation, neurodegenerative and chronic kidney, liver, lung disorders are the top of chronic diseases, and treatments have faced several limitations as the reasons are based on multifactorial pathology, biological barrier, interpatient disease heterogeneity, poor accumulation of drugs in the lesion sites, general toxicity as well as the absent of drug-release mechanisms responding to changing microenvironment of the lesion site.The innovative smart drug delivery platforms of multi-stimuli-responsive nanoparticles have emerged in the field of drug delivery for combining two or more endogenous and/or exogenous stimuli to realize targeted release, spatially controlled drug release, and temporally controlled release.The endogenous stimuli, including decreased pH, redox gradient, ROS, enzyme, hypoxia, glucose, and ATP, can be combined with external stimuli, including temperature, light, magnetic field, and ultrasound, to trigger targeted delivery of nanoparticles and enhance the specificity of drug release.In the present work, the principles, classification, design principles, material selections, and engineering strategies for the development of multi-stimuli-responsive nanoparticles, including the sequential stimulation and co-stimulation mechanisms, the cascaded responsive nanocarriers, and the charge-reversal and size-transformable nanocarriers were critically presented.Different nanoparticle systems, including polymer nanoparticles, micelles, nanogels, liposomes, lipid-polymer hybrid nanoparticles, mesoporous silica nanoparticles, magnetic nanoparticles, metal-organic frameworks, and biomimetic systems, were highlighted.Stimuli-responsive building units and self-assembly techniques for them were also reviewed.The disease applications of several models, including cancer, diabetes, cardiovascular diseases, inflammatory diseases, neurological disorders, kidney diseases, hepatic diseases, and lung diseases, were evaluated and debated.Despite encouraging developments, challenges remain for clinical translation, such as biological variability, uncertain trigger intensity, off-target delivery, premature leakage of drugs, formation of a protein corona, and immune rejection; difficulties in formulation and scale-up production, reproducibility, stability, uncertainty in toxicity, and changing regulatory guidelines.The responsive nanoparticles, in the light of developing new, complex designs, may eventually transition from "smart" but static nanocarriers to "intelligent and dynamic" nanotherapeutics, which must also, in parallel, consider balancing the complex responses with ease of preparation, safety and reliability as well as clinical potential.

papers.title: Formulation, Statistical Optimization, and In Vitro Characterization of Mucoadhesive Buccal Films of Propranolol Hydrochloride
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: The present study aimed to formulate, optimize, and evaluate a controlled-release mucoadhesive buccal film of propranolol hydrochloride for sustained systemic drug delivery while avoiding hepatic first-pass metabolism.A 3² full factorial design was employed to investigate the effects of HPMC E15 and Carbopol 934P on two critical quality attributes: mucoadhesive strength and cumulative drug release after 8 hours.The optimized formulation was characterized for its physicochemical, mechanical, mucoadhesive, and solid-state properties.FTIR and differential scanning calorimetry studies confirmed the compatibility of propranolol hydrochloride with the selected excipients, indicating the absence of significant chemical or thermal interactions.Scanning electron microscopy revealed a smooth, homogeneous, and non-porous film surface, while X-ray diffraction demonstrated the conversion of the crystalline drug into an amorphous form within the polymeric matrix.Statistical analysis using analysis of variance confirmed that both formulation variables significantly influenced the measured responses (p < 0.05), with Carbopol 934P exerting the greatest effect on enhancing mucoadhesive strength and controlling drug release.The optimized buccal film exhibited satisfactory mechanical properties with improved flexibility due to the incorporation of propylene glycol as a plasticizer.In vitro dissolution studies demonstrated a controlled biphasic drug release profile over an 8-hour period.Drug release kinetics followed the Korsmeyer-Peppas model with a diffusional exponent (n) of 0.68, indicating an anomalous (non-Fickian) transport mechanism governed by the combined effects of drug diffusion and polymer swelling.Overall, the optimized buccal film demonstrated excellent physicochemical stability, mechanical integrity, and sustained drug release characteristics, indicating its potential as an effective and reproducible buccal drug delivery system for the systemic administration of propranolol hydrochloride.

papers.title: Isolation and Characterization of Type I Collagen from Decapterus macarellus: An Underutilized Source for Biomaterial Development
authors: B. G. D. N. K. De Silva
papers.journal: Asian Journal of Fisheries and Aquatic Research
papers.abstract: Marine-derived collagen represents a potential alternative to conventional mammalian collagen and offers opportunities for the utilisation of underused fish resources. This study investigated the extraction and physicochemical characterisation of acid-soluble collagen from whole Decapterus macarellus and its flesh, skin and other waste fractions. Collagen was extracted using alkaline pretreatment, demineralisation, acetic acid extraction and salt precipitation. The recovered materials were characterised using scanning electron microscopy (SEM), Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, ultraviolet–visible spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction (XRD), thermal analysis and humidity-regain measurements. Collagen yields from flesh, skin and waste fractions were 25.24 ± 5.21%, 8.51 ± 1.54% and 15.45 ± 2.95%, respectively, with flesh producing the highest yield among the separated tissues. SEM examination of whole-fish collagen revealed an entangled fibrous structure. FTIR spectra exhibited characteristic amide A, B, I, II and III bands, supporting the presence of collagen-associated functional groups. Ultraviolet–visible spectra showed characteristic absorption maxima and limited absorption in the 250–280 nm region. XRD analysis yielded d-spacing values of 0.2829, 0.2834 and 0.2799 nm for flesh, skin and waste collagen, respectively, consistent with structural features associated with the collagen helix. Thermal and humidity-regain analyses indicated variation among the extracted fractions. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of recovering collagen from different tissues of D. macarellus and provide preliminary physicochemical evidence supporting its further investigation as a source of collagen-based biomaterials.

papers.title: Synthesis, Characterization and Thermal Properties of Homomer and Copolymers of N-Phenylmaleimide with Methyl Methacrylate
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: N-Phenylmaleimide (NPMI) was synthesized and subsequently copolymerized with methyl methacrylate (MMA) through free-radical polymerization in tetrahydrofuran (THF), benzoyl peroxide (BPO) as initiators. The synthesized materials were characterized by Fourier-transform infrared (FT-IR) spectroscopy, proton nuclear magnetic resonance (1H NMR) spectroscopy, solubility analysis, and intrinsic-viscosity measurements. Gel permeation chromatography (GPC) was employed to determine molecular weight, whereas Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) was used to evaluate thermal behaviour. The NPMI-based homopolymer and NPMI–MMA copolymer (CPMI) was obtained in yields of 42.6% and 47.0%, respectively, with corresponding intrinsic-viscosity values of 0.042 and 0.070 dL/g. Spectroscopic findings confirmed the consumption of the maleimide carbon–carbon double bond during polymerization while demonstrating that the imide-ring structure remained intact. The copolymer exhibited favourable solubility in several organic solvents .TGA indicated a single-stage degradation pattern and satisfactory thermal stability. Overall, the results establish that NPMI–MMA copolymers possess favourable physicochemical and thermal properties, supporting their potential use in advanced polymeric applications.

papers.title: Effect of glass fiber/talc hybridization ratio on the viscoelastic, thermal, and morphological properties of polypropylene composites
papers.abstract: This study investigates the effects of systematically redistributing a constant nominal reinforcement content of 40 wt% between short glass fibers (GF) and particulate talc on the viscoelastic, thermal, crystallization, and morphological properties of polypropylene (PP) composites. Commercial PP compounds containing 40 wt% GF (GF40) and 40 wt% talc (TF40) were melt-blended at GF40/TF40 ratios of 100/0, 0/100, 25/75, 75/25, and 50/50, while maintaining an approximately constant PP matrix content of 60 wt%. Dynamic Mechanical Analysis showed that the GF-only formulation exhibited the highest storage modulus, approximately 4100 MPa, whereas increasing talc content generally reduced viscous energy dissipation. Thermogravimetric Analysis indicated that the talc-rich C2 and C3 formulations exhibited closely comparable delayed degradation onset. C3 showed the highest measured T_(5%)and T_(10%)values of 437.02 and 447.25 ℃, respectively, while C2 exhibited corresponding values of 435.35 and 446.55 ℃, indicating a formulation-dependent response rather than a simple monotonic talc barrier effect. Differential Scanning Calorimetry showed that C1 and the GF-dominant hybrid C4 exhibited the highest and nearly comparable PP matrix crystallinity values of 43.3% and 43.0%, respectively. Scanning Electron Microscopy observations revealed formulation-dependent fracture-surface features, including exposed fibers, particle-rich regions, and localized voids. Overall, the results demonstrate that redistributing a constant reinforcement content between GF and talc provides a practical approach for tailoring stiffness, energy dissipation, degradation behavior, and crystallization performance in commercially compounded PP systems.

papers.title: Lipid Extract from Ulva ohnoi Algae: Chemical Characterization, Antibacterial Potential, and Cytotoxicity in the Search for New Agents Against MDR Infections
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance is a critical global concern. This study explored the lipid extract (LE) of Ulva ohnoi regarding its chemical composition, antibacterial activity, and cytotoxicity against multidrug-resistant (MDR) microorganisms. The LE was characterized by GC–MS, thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), and differential scanning calorimetry (DSC). Antibacterial efficacy was determined by Minimum Inhibitory Concentration (MIC) and Minimum Bactericidal Concentration (MBC) against MDR isolates: Acinetobacter baumannii, Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Staphylococcus aureus, and coagulase-negative Staphylococci (CoNS). Cytotoxicity was evaluated in murine fibroblast (L929) and bovine renal fibroblast (MDBK) cells using MTT, Neutral Red (NR), Lactate Dehydrogenase (LDH), and hemolytic activity (HA) assays. Lipid characterization revealed palmitic acid (63.62%) and oleic acid (21.01%) as major components. TGA indicated 88% mass loss, and DSC showed no amorphous/crystalline domains. LE showed favorable MIC values against S. aureus and CoNS (1.33 mg/mL) and against A. baumannii and E. coli (2 mg/mL), indicating moderate antibacterial activity typical of an unfractionated crude extract. MBC results indicated bacteriostatic activity (1–8 mg/mL). The extract was cytotoxic to L929 and MDBK cells at concentrations close to its MIC (IC₅₀ 0.25–1.95 mg/mL) but well tolerated by blood cells (HA IC50 4.705 mg/mL). U. ohnoi LE extends, rather than establishes, the previously reported antibacterial potential of Ulva lipids through comprehensive chemical characterization and MDR-isolate evaluation. However, low selectivity indices (SI < 10) indicate that the LE does not yet present an adequate therapeutic window, reinforcing the need for bioassay-guided purification. Nevertheless, it is a starting point for developing new antibacterial agents. Graphical Abstract
papers.summary: Cytotoxicity was evaluated in murine fibroblast (L929) and bovine renal fibroblast (MDBK) cells using MTT, Neutral Red (NR), Lactate Dehydrogenase (LDH), and hemolytic activity (HA) assays. TGA indicated 88% mass loss, and DSC showed no amorphous/crystalline domains. MBC results indicated bacteriostatic activity (1–8 mg/mL).

papers.title: Predictive Value of Inflammatory and Coagulation Biomarkers for Hemodynamic Instability During Spinal Anesthesia in Major Orthopedic Surgery: A Prospective Cohort Study
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Background: Hemodynamic instability after spinal anaesthesia is a common worry at the time of surgery in major orthopaedic surgery patients. Dysregulations of inflammatory and coagulation have potential effects on vascular responsiveness and can play a role in post-spinal hypotension. The aim of this study was to assess the predictive role of some selected inflammatory and coagulation markers for hemodynamic instability following spinal anesthesia. Methods: This prospective cohort study included 120 adult patients of both genders undergoing major orthopedic surgery under spinal anesthesia from January 2022 to January 2023. C-reactive protein (CRP), interleukin-6 (IL-6), neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet count, prothrombin time, activated partial thromboplastin time, fibrinogen and D-dimer were assessed preoperatively. Hemodynamic instability was characterized by a decrease in SBP of 20% or more or MBP of <65 mmHg or the need for vasopressor therapy. Multivariable logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic analysis was done. Results: Hemodynamic instability occurred in 45 patients (37.5%). The levels of CRP, IL-6, NLR, fibrinogen and Ddimer were significantly higher in patients with instability. After adjustment, CRP ≥6 mg/L (aOR 2.46; 95% CI 1.125.41), NLR ≥4.0 (aOR 2.31; 95% CI 1.06–5.04), D-dimer ≥0.60 mg/L (aOR 2.72; 95% CI 1.21–6.12), and lower baseline mean arterial pressure independently predicted instability. The AUC of the combined clinical-biomarker model was 0.84. Conclusion: Preoperative CRP, NLR and D-dimer can be useful to predict the hemodynamic instability after spinal anesthesia in orthopedic patients and can help to identify high-risk patients in an early stage.
papers.summary: Background: Hemodynamic instability after spinal anaesthesia is a common worry at the time of surgery in major orthopaedic surgery patients. The aim of this study was to assess the predictive role of some selected inflammatory and coagulation markers for hemodynamic instability following spinal anesthesia. Results: Hemodynamic instability occurred in 45 patients (37.5%).

papers.title: Zn/Al‐ NO 3 Layered Double Hydroxide as Alternative Activator for Nitrile Rubber Vulcanization: Effect of the Accelerator‐to‐Sulfur Ratio on Curing Kinetics and Network Properties
authors: Marcus Vinícius Alves Sampaio de Souza
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Reducing zinc content in rubber formulations remains an important challenge due to environmental concerns associated with the use of zinc oxide (ZnO) as part of vulcanization systems. Zinc‐containing layered double hydroxides (Zn/Al‐LDHs) offer an alternative approach to incorporating zinc into lamellar structure and have been investigated as both vulcanization activators and fillers. However, the curing behavior of unmodified Zn/Al‐NO 3 LDH in conventional nitrile rubber (NBR) remains insufficiently understood. In this study, Zn/Al‐NO 3 LDH was evaluated as an alternative low‐zinc vulcanization activator for nitrile rubber (NBR) as a replacement for the ZnO/stearic acid system. Conventional (A/S = 0.6) and efficient (A/S = 3.0) sulfur‐curing systems were compared. In the conventional system, the LDH decreased the apparent Ea from 90.81 to 70.95 kJ.mol −1 and reduced the pre‐exponential factor by approximately two orders of magnitude. Tensile strength remained comparable, whereas tear strength decreased by approximately 14%. Thermogravimetric analysis showed a slight increase in the onset degradation temperature for the LDH‐containing formulations. Based on nominal compositions, replacing the ZnO/stearic acid activation system with Zn/Al‐NO 3 LDH corresponded to an estimated 71% reduction in zinc loading. Environmental benefits cannot be inferred from this reduction because zinc release, bioavailability, and ecotoxicological effects were not evaluated.
papers.summary: ABSTRACT Reducing zinc content in rubber formulations remains an important challenge due to environmental concerns associated with the use of zinc oxide (ZnO) as part of vulcanization systems. Thermogravimetric analysis showed a slight increase in the onset degradation temperature for the LDH‐containing formulations. Environmental benefits cannot be inferred from this reduction because zinc release, bioavailability, and ecotoxicological effects were not evaluated.

papers.title: Formulation, Development, and Evaluation of Fast-Disintegrating Tablets of Meloxicam Solid Dispersion for Enhanced Solubility and Dissolution
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Introduction: Meloxicam is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) with poor aqueous solubility (BCS Class II) which exhibits dissolution limited absorption. The use of solid dispersion technology along with fast disintegrating tablets is a promising way to enhance its pharmaceutical properties. Aim: To formulate, develop, and evaluate fast-disintegrating tablets containing meloxicam solid dispersion for enhanced aqueous solubility and in vitro drug dissolution. Methodology: Meloxicam–Poloxamer 188 solid dispersions were prepared at drug-to-polymer ratios of 1:1, 1:2, and 1:3 using the solvent evaporation method. The drug content, saturation solubility, drug/excipient compatibility, and solid-state properties were characterized of prepared dispersions using UV spectrophotometry, FTIR, DSC and XRD. Seven formulations of fast disintegrating tablets (F1–F7) were prepared by direct compression and tested for pre compression and post compression parameters, disintegration time, in vitro dissolution and accelerated stability. Results: The solid dispersion 1:2 had the highest saturation solubility of 0.44 ± 0.03 mg/mL in phosphate buffer (pH 6.8) which is around 11 times higher than that of pure meloxicam (0.040 mg/mL). There was no major incompatibility as revealed by FTIR and XRD indicated reduced crystallinity. Formulation F2 had the fastest disintegration time (36.63 ± 0.32 seconds), drug content of 99.12 ± 0.12%, and maximum cumulative drug release of 97.18 ± 2.84% in 60 minutes. The accelerated stability testing of three months showed that the drug release was still 96.09 ± 1.71%. Conclusion: Using Poloxamer 188 as a solid dispersion technique was able to increase the solubility of meloxicam, and the optimized fast disintegration tablet showed good dissolution and short term stability. Further in vivo investigations are necessary to establish bioavailability improvements.
papers.summary: Aim: To formulate, develop, and evaluate fast-disintegrating tablets containing meloxicam solid dispersion for enhanced aqueous solubility and in vitro drug dissolution. The accelerated stability testing of three months showed that the drug release was still 96.09 ± 1.71%. Conclusion: Using Poloxamer 188 as a solid dispersion technique was able to increase the solubility of meloxicam, and the optimized fast disintegration tablet showed good dissolution and short term stability.

papers.title: BEYOND SOLVENTS: SOLID-STATE ENGINEERING STRATEGIES FOR SOLUBILITY ENHANCEMENT OF POORLY WATER-SOLUBLE DRUGS
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Background: Poor aqueous solubility of active pharmaceutical ingredients remains a major challenge in pharmaceutical development, as it can lead to slow dissolution, inadequate drug absorption, variable bioavailability, and reduced therapeutic performance. Conventional solubility enhancement techniques, including micronization, solvent-based solid dispersion, and the use of solubilizing agents, may involve limitations related to solvent consumption, processing complexity, physical instability, and environmental sustainability. Mechanochemistry has emerged as a promising solid-state engineering approach that uses mechanical energy to modify the physicochemical properties of drug substances, often with reduced or no solvent use. Objective: This review aims to explore mechanochemical approaches for enhancing the solubility and dissolution performance of poorly water-soluble drugs. It emphasizes the fundamental mechanisms, major processing technologies, formulation strategies, and recent developments that support the application of mechanochemistry in pharmaceutical formulation development. Methods: The review examines mechanochemical techniques, including mortar–pestle grinding, ball milling, liquid-assisted grinding, mechanochemical cocrystallization, co-amorphization, and polymer-assisted solid-state processing. It discusses the influence of drug properties, polymeric carriers, coformers, drug-to-carrier ratios, and processing parameters on formulation performance. Analytical and characterization techniques, including Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy, powder X-ray diffraction, differential scanning calorimetry, and microscopic methods, are considered alongside solubility measurements, dissolution testing, and physical stability assessment. Results: Mechanochemical processing offers considerable potential for improving the apparent solubility and dissolution rate of poorly water-soluble drugs through particle-size reduction, crystal lattice disruption, defect formation, amorphization, and modification of drug–excipient interactions. The effectiveness of these approaches depends on formulation composition, processing conditions, and the physical properties of the resulting solid. The review also highlights challenges associated with recrystallization, moisture sensitivity, process reproducibility, and the translation of laboratory-scale methods to industrial manufacturing. Emerging applications of process analytical technology, predictive modelling, and continuous processing provide opportunities to improve process control and scalability. Conclusion: Mechanochemistry represents a versatile and potentially sustainable strategy for improving the pharmaceutical performance of poorly water-soluble drugs. Its advantages include the potential to reduce solvent consumption, minimize waste, and enable targeted solid-state modifications. However, successful implementation requires systematic formulation optimization, comprehensive characterization, long-term stability evaluation, and reliable scale-up strategies. Further research into standardized protocols, quality control, and industrial processing is essential to establish mechanochemistry as a reproducible and practical platform for pharmaceutical development.

It emphasizes the fundamental mechanisms, major processing technologies, formulation strategies, and recent developments that support the application of mechanochemistry in pharmaceutical formulation development. Analytical and characterization techniques, including Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy, powder X-ray diffraction, differential scanning calorimetry, and microscopic methods, are considered alongside solubility measurements, dissolution testing, and physical stability assessment.

papers.title: Preparation-dependent oxygen release and apparent carbon deposition of Cu–Fe/ZrO2 oxygen carriers during wheat straw chemical looping conversion
papers.abstract: Cu–Fe/ZrO 2 composite oxygen carriers with identical nominal compositions were prepared by mechanical mixing (MM), impregnation (IM), and sol–gel synthesis (SG) to investigate how preparation route affects oxygen release, cyclic stability, gas-product distribution, and apparent carbon deposition during wheat straw chemical looping conversion. Oxygen-release behavior was evaluated by thermogravimetric cycling at 900 °C under N 2 with air regeneration at 700 °C, and the carriers were characterized by XRD, SEM, and N 2 physisorption before and after cycling. Fixed-bed tests were subsequently conducted with wheat straw to quantify gas yields, gas-phase carbon conversion, and apparent carbon deposition. SG exhibited the lowest onset oxygen-release temperature (741.5 °C) and the highest apparent oxygen-release capacity (3.38 wt%). After 20 release–reoxidation cycles, its capacity remained 3.35 wt%, corresponding to 99.11% retention. In the first fixed-bed cycle, SG achieved a gas-phase carbon conversion of 79.17%, with CO 2 and CH 4 yields of 24.70 and 0.75 mmol g −1 , respectively. After 20 cycles, its gas-phase carbon conversion remained 78.71%, while apparent carbon deposition was 1.84 mg g −1 , 63.8% lower than that of MM. In contrast, in the first fixed-bed cycle, IM produced the highest H 2 and syngas yields among the three carriers, reaching 7.56 and 13.71 mmol g −1 , respectively. These results demonstrate that preparation route governs the balance between oxygen availability, cyclic stability, carbon accumulation, and syngas preservation in Cu–Fe/ZrO 2 oxygen carriers.
papers.summary: Cu–Fe/ZrO 2 composite oxygen carriers with identical nominal compositions were prepared by mechanical mixing (MM), impregnation (IM), and sol–gel synthesis (SG) to investigate how preparation route affects oxygen release, cyclic stability, gas-product distribution, and apparent carbon deposition during wheat straw chemical looping conversion. Oxygen-release behavior was evaluated by thermogravimetric cycling at 900 °C under N 2 with air regeneration at 700 °C, and the carriers were characterized by XRD, SEM, and N 2 physisorption before and after cycling. These results demonstrate that preparation route governs the balance between oxygen availability, cyclic stability, carbon accumulation, and syngas preservation in Cu–Fe/ZrO 2 oxygen carriers.

papers.title: Defect-Mediated Electronic Structure Engineering of Green-Synthesized ZnO Nanoparticles Using Citrus sinensis Peel Extract for Enhanced Photocatalytic Degradation of Reactive Red 120
papers.abstract: Abstract Zinc oxide (ZnO) is a promising wide-bandgap semiconductor for photocatalytic applications, but its large bandgap limits solar light utilization. In this work, ZnO nanoparticles were synthesized via a green route using Citrus sinensis peel extract as a phytochemical-mediated reducing and stabilizing agent. X-ray diffraction confirmed single-phase hexagonal wurtzite ZnO with an average crystallite size of 17.7 nm, while scanning eelctron microscopy (SEM) and energy-dispersive x-ray spectroscopy (EDS) verified nanoparticle formation without detectable impurities. N $$_2$$ 2 adsorption–desorption analysis showed a specific surface area comparable to commercial ZnO, indicating that surface area differences are unlikely to govern the observed performance gap. Thermogravimetric analysis indicated a small amount of residual phytochemical-derived organic species. Diffuse reflectance spectroscopy revealed a bandgap reduction from approximately 3.1 eV (commercial ZnO) to 2.7 eV (green-synthesized ZnO), with Urbach energy analysis providing quantitative evidence of an elevated density of localized sub-gap states. Photocatalytic degradation of Reactive Red 120 under ultraviolet (UV) irradiation reached approximately 95% removal after 90 min, following pseudo-first-order kinetics ( $$k = 2.0\times 10^{-2}$$ k = 2.0 × 10 - 2 min $$^{-1}$$ - 1 ). Scavenger experiments showed that both hydroxyl and superoxide radicals participate, with superoxide playing the dominant role. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy revealed a marked decrease in charge-transfer resistance under illumination, while Mott–Schottky analysis showed a substantial negative shift of the flat-band potential under operating conditions, providing an electrochemically grounded explanation for the superoxide dominance. Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy confirmed dye adsorption followed by oxidative degradation during irradiation. The combined structural, optical, textural, electrochemical, and photocatalytic results demonstrate that phytochemical-assisted synthesis effectively tunes the optoelectronic properties of ZnO while providing a sustainable route to high-performance photocatalysts.

Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy revealed a marked decrease in charge-transfer resistance under illumination, while Mott–Schottky analysis showed a substantial negative shift of the flat-band potential under operating conditions, providing an electrochemically grounded explanation for the superoxide dominance. The combined structural, optical, textural, electrochemical, and photocatalytic results demonstrate that phytochemical-assisted synthesis effectively tunes the optoelectronic properties of ZnO while providing a sustainable route to high-performance photocatalysts.

papers.title: Formulation and Evaluation of Withaferin A Extract-Loaded Transethosomal Buccal Film for Enhanced Drug Delivery
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: The present study aimed to formulate and evaluate Withaferin A extract-loaded transethosomal buccal films for controlled and prolonged drug delivery. Withaferin A, a bioactive constituent of Withania somnifera, has limited aqueous solubility, which may affect its dissolution and delivery. Transethosomes were developed using soya lecithin and sodium deoxycholate and were incorporated into mucoadhesive buccal films prepared using hydroxypropyl methylcellulose K15M and Carbopol 934. Nine transethosomal formulations (T1–T9) and nine buccal film formulations (F1–F9) were prepared and evaluated. The optimized transethosomal formulation, T5, exhibited a particle size of 142.8 ± 1.74 nm, polydispersity index of 0.198 ± 0.008, zeta potential of −31.6 ± 1.0 mV, entrapment efficiency of 91.6 ± 1.18%, and drug loading of 7.24 ± 0.16%. Among the prepared films, F3 showed the most suitable overall characteristics, including a thickness of 0.134 ± 0.004 mm, folding endurance of 148 ± 3 folds, surface pH of 6.51 ± 0.06, drug content of 98.2 ± 0.8%, and mucoadhesive strength of 29.6 ± 0.7 g. The optimized film released 96.4% of the extract over 12 hours. Release kinetic analysis showed the best fit with the Higuchi model (R² = 0.989), while the Korsmeyer–Peppas exponent of approximately 0.67 suggested anomalous or nonFickian release. Three-month stability studies showed acceptable formulation characteristics under the tested storage conditions. These findings indicate that Withaferin A extract-loaded transethosomal buccal films may provide a promising approach for controlled drug delivery. Further ex-vivo permeation and in-vivo studies are required to establish their absorption and therapeutic performance.
